surface: A column summary row: telling its cells from a data row's, a read-only summary beside an editable one, and a summary recalculated after an edit to its column.

steps.note: A4, the last data row, before the summary row. The column headers are letters (`A`, `B`, `C`), so no header word satisfies the summary group of the later steps. Finding: VoiceOver says nothing on this first arrow key, on both browsers.

A5 is the summary of column A: the sum of the four data rows, 10, calculated by the plugin into the last row. The grid marks the summary cell with a class (`columnSummaryResult`) only, so a reader should say it is a summary before a user takes 10 for a data value. The cell is read only (the plugin's default), and it carries aria-readonly. Finding: every reader reads `10` as a plain cell; none says it is a summary, and none says it is read only.

Enter on the read-only summary opens no editor, and the selection stays on the last row. Nothing is required: the transcript records what a reader says when Enter does nothing. Every reader says nothing, so the user gets no word that the cell cannot be edited.
B5 is the summary of column B, 100, which the fixture configures `readOnly: false`: the same summary fact, without the read-only state. Finding: as on A5, no reader says it is a summary.

B4, a data cell the summary below it adds up. NVDA with Firefox said nothing on this step and on open-editor in the proof run and read both in the recording: a late phrase the lane lost, not the grid's.

Enter opens the text editor on B4: its value and its editable role, the words grid-core's open-editor takes. Finding: VoiceOver with WebKit says the value alone (`40`), without the field's role, as in grid-core.
Selects the editor's text, so the typed value replaces it.
The new value. Nothing is required: a reader's echo of typed keys is its own setting.
Enter commits 50 and moves the selection one row down (enterMoves), onto the summary, which the plugin recalculated: 10 + 20 + 30 + 50. Every reader reads `110`.
